maya: Hey team — onboarding Orbit9b (int4) is blowing up on canary with OOMs at tail generation spikes. Repro steps below, logs attached. Anyone seen similar fragmentation patterns?
kevin: saw the OOMs in the canary. pattern: large max_new_tokens + concurrent streaming -> mem surge, then fragment.
oliver: exact failure: allocation failed for 64MB tensor during kv cache growth. allocator: curtis-slab-v2 shows lots of small free slabs.
ciara: can you paste the trace/log?
maya: sure — snippet from runtime: 
```
[E 13:22:11] alloc failed: requested 67108864 bytes
[E 13:22:11] kv_cache_grow: new_seq_len 1024 current_slots 2048
[E 13:22:11] slab_free_count: 18342 small_slots avg 4kb
[E 13:22:11] OOM -> fall back to model-compat-fallback
```
jen: interesting — looks like large contiguous allocs are scarce. two approaches: reduce per-request max_new_tokens, or reserve contiguous slots at startup.
kevin: we already have reserve_slots param but Orbit9b seems to need more headroom because int4 kernel temp buffers are spiky. current reserved_slots=1. propose reserved_slots=3 for canary.
ciara: Also consider adaptive max_new_tokens per-route. Many calls are short; default 512 is too aggressive. Could change model default to 256 and let route override.
oliver: batching settings: we saw higher throughput but more fragmentation under big microbatches. Try reducing max_batch_time_ms and shrink microbatch cap so we don't coalesce huge sequences together.
maya: action items I propose: 1) change model default max_new_tokens=256 (canary) 2) set reserver_slots=3 3) lower batch window from 12ms -> 6ms for this model 4) enable prefetched-kv compaction (experimental)
jen: sounds good. small note: compaction code path is opt-in via runtime flag --enable-kv-compaction. It trades CPU for contiguous memory. Should be okay on canary nodes.
kevin: I'll push a canary config change:
```
``nctl apply model-config orbit9b --set default_max_new_tokens=256 --set reserver_slots=3 --set batch_window_ms=6 --set kv_compaction=on
```
maya: typo in that CLI: "reserver_slots" -> "reserve_slots"
kevin: oops, fixed. thanks.
deploy-bot: Triggering canary rollout for orbit9b config at 1754123620 by kevin
ciara: parallel test plan: 1) 5000 short-chat requests (avg new_tokens=60) 2) 100 long-gen requests (new_tokens=900) 3) mixed concurrency 50. check memory curves and eviction counts.
maya: define success: no OOMs in 1h stress run and 95p latency within 1.3x baseline. Also no quality regressions in 100 eval prompts.
oliver: for extra safety, add a soft gate: if OOMs spike, move traffic to fallback smaller model (orbit7b) via routing policy.
kevin: deploying now. I'll post results in 15m. :mag:
maya: quick heuristic we can try if compaction isn't enough: per-process slab trim on idle via `malloc_trim(0)` after batch flush. Could reduce fragmentation without major code churn.
jen: true, but test first — trim can cause perf hiccups.
kevin: canary up. initial smoke shows memory smoother, but one transient allocation warning at 15:07.
maya: keep watching. if that warning turns to OOM we'll roll back.
ciara: if stable for 30m, we can promote reserve_slots as default for orbit family.
kevin: will update status in this thread. :thumbsup:
